officialTitle: Elacestrant (oral selective estrogen receptor degrader) Versus Standard Endocrine Therapy for Estrogen Receptor-Positive, Human Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor 2-Negative Advanced Breast Cancer: Results From the Randomized Phase III EMERALD Trial
setting: Advanced disease after one or two lines of endocrine therapy including a CDK4/6 inhibitor

design.blinding: Open-label; PFS by blinded independent central review
primaryEndpoints: PFS (BICR) in patients with detectable ESR1 mutation
design.notes: Required prior CDK4/6 inhibitor; one-two lines of endocrine therapy and ≤1 chemotherapy. Comparator: standard-of-care endocrine monotherapy. 239 patients assigned to elacestrant and 238 to standard of care.

clinicalQuestion: Is the oral SERD elacestrant superior to standard endocrine monotherapy after CDK4/6 inhibitor-based therapy in ER-positive/HER2-negative advanced breast cancer, overall and in ESR1-mutated disease?

pico.population: ER-positive/HER2-negative advanced breast cancer after one-two lines of endocrine therapy, prior CDK4/6 inhibitor required, ≤1 chemotherapy
pico.outcomes: Primary: PFS by BICR in all patients and in ESR1-mutated patients. Safety

arms.label: Elacestrant
arms.doseSourceQuote: Patients were randomly assigned to elacestrant 400 mg orally once daily or standard-of-care (SOC) endocrine monotherapy.

publications.title: Elacestrant (oral selective estrogen receptor degrader) Versus Standard Endocrine Therapy for Estrogen Receptor-Positive, Human Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor 2-Negative Advanced Breast Cancer: Results From the Randomized Phase III EMERALD Trial.
publications.label: Primary analysis

outcomes.sourceQuote: PFS was prolonged in all patients (hazard ratio = 0.70; 95% CI, 0.55 to 0.88;= .002)
and patients withmutation (hazard ratio = 0.55; 95% CI, 0.39 to 0.77;= .0005)

safety.sourceQuote: Treatment-related grade 3/4 adverse events occurred in 7.2% receiving elacestrant and 3.1% receiving SOC.

safety.description: Treatment-related adverse events leading to discontinuation
safety.sourceQuote: Treatment-related adverse events leading to treatment discontinuations were 3.4% in the elacestrant arm versus 0.9% in SOC.
Nausea of any grade occurred in 35.0% receiving elacestrant and 18.8% receiving SOC (grade 3/4, 2.5% and 0.9%, respectively).

strengths: Randomised phase III trial with PFS by blinded independent central review
All patients had prior CDK4/6 inhibitor, matching the contemporary second-line population
limitations: Comparator was endocrine monotherapy, not a combination regimen
Median PFS values not reported in the abstract

clinicalImplications.text: Supports elacestrant after CDK4/6 inhibitor-based therapy in ER-positive/HER2-negative advanced breast cancer, with greater relative benefit in ESR1-mutated disease, making ESR1 mutation testing at progression relevant.

tumourBoardPearl.text: The larger relative benefit was in ESR1-mutated disease — consider ESR1 testing at progression on a CDK4/6 inhibitor before choosing endocrine therapy.

curation.notes: Numbers transcribed from the PubMed abstract of PMID 35584336. PubMed text strips the italic gene symbol ESR1 ('withmutation') and the 'P' before P values ('= .002', '= .0005'); P values therefore not transcribed into pValue. Sponsor and registry ID not printed in the abstract and omitted.
